drafted_from: tool:collect-and-rank-viewer-questions's row (tools/collect-and-rank-viewer-questions/tool-rows.json), do-work/candidates.py, do-work/rank.py and test/viewer-questions.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Find the questions in the forum posts and video comments saved in ./viewer-questions, using my sample-baker settings row, and rank them into my buckets." It runs the candidates script on your computer, then rank with your settings file, and tells you how many questions it found and which bucket each fits.

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON. For this tool the settings hold your buckets, bucket codes, overrides, inferred questions, package readings and reach rules.

instructions: 1. Pour the two example settings rows into the settings list you already keep (see pour), or make list:settings from them; replace the buckets with your own topics and words. Keep status active: a retired row is refused.

2. Put your forum posts (forum-posts.jsonl, kept by tool:keep-forum-posts-from-a-public-archive) and video comments (youtube-comments/*.info.json, or comments.jsonl kept by tool:keep-channels-latest-videos-and-captions) in one folder, for example ./viewer-questions, with a raw/ folder beside them.

3. Say "Find the questions my viewers really ask". The AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: tool:collect-and-rank-viewer-questions}, installs sentence-transformers and numpy, reads your settings row with tool:read-a-tool-setting and writes it to a file.

4. The AI runs the candidates script (python3 tools/collect-and-rank-viewer-questions/do-work/candidates.py <folder> <out.tsv>) and then rank.py with the settings file; read the last JSON line of each: {"result": {...}} or {"error": what to fix}.

5. Pick the questions worth keeping (picks.txt), then have the AI run embed_moments, build_library with the picks and settings, and apply_gate with your copy rules (tool:check-copy); it writes the questions with their frequency and answers back as rows of your library and tells you which have no answer yet.

worked_examples.title: Five question candidates found in two forum posts and two videos' comments
worked_examples.ask: Find the questions my viewers really ask in the posts and comments saved in ./viewer-questions.
worked_examples.given: From tools/collect-and-rank-viewer-questions/test/viewer-questions.test.mjs: ./viewer-questions holds forum-posts.jsonl (post p1 titled "How do I keep my starter alive on holiday?" whose body adds "Also why does my dough tear when I stretch it?", and post p2 whose body asks "How can I get a more open crumb in my loaf?"), youtube-comments/vid0000001.info.json (a comment "What should I feed my starter every single day?" with 120 likes and "Nice video") and comments.jsonl (video vid0000002: "Why does my bread go flat in the oven every time?"), with ./viewer-questions/raw/ made. The AI runs, from the folder holding the trillion-workshop clone: python3 trillion-workshop/tools/collect-and-rank-viewer-questions/do-work/candidates.py ./viewer-questions ./viewer-questions/raw/candidates.tsv.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result": {"candidates": 5, "posts": 2, "videos": 2, "out": "./viewer-questions/raw/candidates.tsv"}} as the last line. candidates.tsv holds ids 0 to 4: the two post sentences about the starter and the dough, the crumb sentence, then the two comment questions, the starter one linked https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vid0000001&lc=c1. "Nice video" is not kept: it ends in no question mark.

pour.how: Name the settings list you already keep and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
